subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should every caller of the public `CronServiceContract.run` be permanently defined as a non-consuming operator run, with scheduler-consuming behavior reserved for private timer and gateway-watcher entries?
rationale: This is a compatibility decision for existing facade callers and persisted cron-state semantics; source review can verify the mechanism but cannot establish the intended long-term public contract.

options.title: Confirm non-consuming public runs
options.body: Adopt the branch's boundary: public `run` records an operator outcome only, while timer and the concrete gateway watcher own scheduler state and one-shot consumption.

options.title: Preserve an explicit consuming facade contract
options.body: Define and document a supported internal/public caller path for intentional scheduler-consuming forced runs, with compatibility tests and access boundaries.

recommendation.title: Confirm non-consuming public runs
recommendation.body: Adopt the branch's boundary: public `run` records an operator outcome only, while timer and the concrete gateway watcher own scheduler state and one-shot consumption.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns adjacent cron scheduling and persisted-state invariants that this PR extends.
